# hush_api_application (Resource)

An API application: a `hush_custom_api_application`'s enabled tools made available to agents through the agent gateways of the deployments it is placed on. The address, headers and credential are the custom app's.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The billing API on the gateway of one deployment, for the finance team, asking
# the user before listing invoices and capping each caller at 100 calls an hour.
resource "hush_api_application" "billing" {
  app_catalog_id = hush_custom_api_application.billing.app_catalog_id
  display_name   = "Billing"
  deployment_ids = [hush_deployment.gateway.id]

  tool_operation {
    name      = "list_invoices"
    operation = "user_consent"
  }
  rate_limit {
    target_type = "app"
    max_calls   = 100
    window      = 3600
  }

  assignment {
    condition {
      match {
        source   = "user"
        property = "groups"
        op       = "in"
        values   = ["finance"]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `app_catalog_id` (String) The custom API app's `app_catalog_id` ('custom-<name>'). It needs an enabled tool. Fixed at creation.
- `deployment_ids` (Set of String) The deployments whose gateways serve the application.
- `display_name` (String) The name the application is shown under. Unique within the organization.

### Optional

- `allowed_agents` (Set of String) Limit the application to these agent types: 'claude-code', 'claude', 'cursor', 'windsurf', 'vscode' and 'openclaw'. Leave unset, or empty, to allow any agent.
- `assign_all` (Boolean) Grant the application to every user of the organization, whatever `assignment` says.
- `assignment` (Block List) A rule granting the application to the users and agents it matches. An agent may use the application when any of the rules matches it; a rule matches when all of its `condition` blocks do. With neither this nor `assign_all`, the application is granted to no one, and users can only request access to it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--assignment))
- `description` (String) A description of the application.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the gateways serve the application. A disabled application keeps its configuration.
- `rate_limit` (Block Set) A cap on how many calls each caller (a user, or a service agent) may make through the gateway: to any of the application's tools, to its tools of one class, or to one tool. A call must fit every limit it matches. One block per target; a limit without a block is removed, including one set elsewhere, such as in the console. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--rate_limit))
- `tool_defaults` (Block List, Max: 1) What the gateway does with a call to a tool of each class, unless `tool_operation` sets the tool's own. Each is 'allow', 'block' or 'user_consent' (ask the user, through the deployment's `hush_agw_consent_methods`). A class left unset keeps what the application has, which starts as allow for read, user_consent for write and block for destructive; removing the block changes nothing. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--tool_defaults))
- `tool_operation` (Block Set) The operation for one tool, overriding its class default. The tool must be one of the application's (see `tools`). A tool without a block takes its class default, so removing a block returns the tool to it, and an override set elsewhere, such as in the console, is removed on the next apply. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--tool_operation))

### Read-Only

- `catalog_display_name` (String) The name the catalog shows for the entry.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `name` (String) The name agents see the application under: its `app_catalog_id`.
- `tools` (List of Object) The custom app's enabled tools. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tools))
- `url` (String) The API's address, from the custom app.

<a id="nestedblock--assignment"></a>
### Nested Schema for `assignment`

Required:

- `condition` (Block List, Min: 1) A condition of the rule. It holds when any of its `match` blocks does. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--assignment--condition))

<a id="nestedblock--assignment--condition"></a>
### Nested Schema for `assignment.condition`

Required:

- `match` (Block List, Min: 1) One comparison of a property of the user or of the agent. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--assignment--condition--match))

<a id="nestedblock--assignment--condition--match"></a>
### Nested Schema for `assignment.condition.match`

Required:

- `op` (String) How the property is compared: 'eq' and 'neq' against `value`, 'in' and 'nin' against `values`.
- `property` (String) The property compared: for 'user', a claim such as 'email' or 'groups'; for 'agent', only 'id'.
- `source` (String) What the property belongs to: 'user' (a claim of the user's identity provider profile, or 'groups' for the groups the user is in) or 'agent'.

Optional:

- `value` (String) The value 'eq' and 'neq' compare against.
- `values` (List of String) The values 'in' and 'nin' compare against. At least one.




<a id="nestedblock--rate_limit"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rate_limit`

Required:

- `max_calls` (Number) The calls allowed at once; they come back one by one over `window`.
- `target_type` (String) 'app', 'group' or 'tool'.
- `window` (Number) Seconds, from 60 to 86400.

Optional:

- `mode` (String) 'block' refuses calls past the limit; 'warn' lets them through and flags them in the activity log.
- `target` (String) For 'group', the class: 'read', 'write' or 'destructive'. For 'tool', the tool's name (see `tools`). Unset for 'app'.


<a id="nestedblock--tool_defaults"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tool_defaults`

Optional:

- `destructive` (String) The operation for tools of class 'destructive'.
- `read` (String) The operation for tools of class 'read'.
- `write` (String) The operation for tools of class 'write'.


<a id="nestedblock--tool_operation"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tool_operation`

Required:

- `name` (String) The tool's name.
- `operation` (String) 'allow', 'block' or 'user_consent'.


<a id="nestedatt--tools"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tools`

Read-Only:

- `description` (String)
- `name` (String)
- `operation` (String)
- `type` (String)

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by the application id.
terraform import hush_api_application.billing app-abc123
```
